D: A mouse detective in 1897 London takes on Professor Ratigan to rescue a kidnapped toymaker.
P: Serve the snacks when Mrs Judson brings in the cheese crumpets.
S: Toasted crumpets under melted cheddar and English mustard
Crumpets toasted, spread with butter and topped with grated cheddar and a little mustard, grilled until bubbling.
Soft boiled eggs wrapped in pork sausage, crumbed and fried
Scotch eggs of soft-boiled eggs wrapped in pork sausage meat, crumbed and fried, with mustard.

Gingerbread cut into toy shapes, baked at 180C for 10 minutes, piped with white icing. Melt 125g butter, 100g brown sugar and 125ml golden syrup together. Sift 375g plain flour with 1 tsp bicarb, 3 tsp ground ginger and 1 tsp cinnamon, then stir in the butter mix and 1 beaten egg. Knead into a dough and chill 30 minutes. Roll to 5mm and cut into toy soldiers, teddies and tops. Bake on lined trays at 180C for 10 minutes. Cool, then pipe with icing of 150g icing sugar and a little egg white.
M: Lamb mince with carrots and peas under mash
Lamb mince with onion, carrot and peas under buttery mash, baked at 200C until golden.
Mouse Queen: "Ah, I just adore Jubilees."

Beef topside roasted at 200C to medium, rested, with Yorkshire puddings, roast potatoes and gravy made from the pan. Rub a 1.5kg beef topside with oil, salt and mustard powder and roast at 200C for 50 minutes for medium. Rest 15 minutes. Roast 1kg parboiled potatoes in hot oil for 50 minutes. Whisk 140g plain flour, 4 eggs and 200ml milk. Heat oil in a 12-hole muffin tin at 230C, pour in the batter and bake 20 minutes without opening the door. Stir 1 tbsp flour into the pan juices, add 300ml beef stock and simmer into gravy.
W: Butter sponge layers with strawberry jam and whipped cream
Two vanilla sponges baked at 180C for 25 minutes, sandwiched with strawberry jam and whipped cream, dusted with icing sugar.
K: Earl Grey tea with honey and lemon juice, over ice

Earl Grey brewed strong and chilled with lemon juice and honey, topped with sparkling water over ice and served with a shortbread finger. Steep 4 Earl Grey tea bags in 600ml boiling water for 5 minutes, remove and stir in 3 tbsp honey. Chill for 2 hours. Add the juice of 3 lemons. Fill 4 glasses with ice and lemon slices, pour in the tea to two thirds full and top with 300ml sparkling water. Serve with shortbread fingers.

dishes.make_ahead: Grate the cheddar and mix with the mustard up to 2 days ahead in the fridge; toast and grill just before serving

steps.text: Grate the cheddar and mix with the mustard.
Toast the crumpets until golden and butter them.
Pile the cheese onto each crumpet.
Grill until bubbling and golden.

dishes.make_ahead: Boil, peel and wrap the eggs up to 1 day ahead and keep them in the fridge; crumb and fry on the day

steps.text: Boil the four eggs, cool and peel.
Boil.
Cool.
Wrap each egg in sausage mince.
Roll in flour, beaten egg and panko.
Fry in the oil at 170C until golden.
Halve and serve with mustard.

veg.make_ahead: Up to 1 day, reheat to serve

steps.text: Boil the four eggs until just set.
Cool and peel.
Mash the vegetarian sausage filling with a handful of the panko.
Wrap each egg in the mixture.
Roll in flour, beaten egg and the rest of the panko.
Fry in the oil at 170C until golden.
Halve and serve with mustard.

dishes.make_ahead: Assemble up to 1 day ahead and keep covered in the fridge; bake from cold and add 15 minutes

steps.text: Dice the onion, grate the carrots and peel the potatoes.
Brown the mince with onion and carrot, add peas and a little water and simmer until thick.
Boil and mash the potatoes with butter.
Spread the mince in a dish and top with mash.
Bake at 200C until golden.

veg.make_ahead: Make the lentil base up to 2 days ahead in the fridge; top with fresh mash and bake on the night

steps.text: Dice the onion, grate the carrots, chop the mushrooms and peel the potatoes.
Brown the mushrooms with the onion and carrot in the oil, add the tomato paste, soy sauce, lentils, peas and stock and simmer until thick.
Boil and mash the potatoes with butter.
Spread the lentils in a dish and top with mash.
Bake at 200C until golden.
Heat the oven to 180C and prepare two tins. Beat the butter and sugar, add the eggs, then fold in the flour.
Bake in two tins.
Cool completely.
Whip the cream. Sandwich the cakes with jam and cream.
Dust the top with icing sugar.

dishes.make_ahead: Steep and chill the tea up to 2 days ahead in the fridge; add the lemon, ice and sparkling water to serve

steps.text: Steep the tea bags for 5 minutes, remove and stir in the honey.
Chill.
Juice three lemons and slice the fourth.
Add the juice to the tea. Fill four glasses with ice and lemon slices, pour in the tea two thirds full and top with sparkling water.
Serve with shortbread fingers.

s.note: Toasted crumpets under melted cheddar and English mustard
s.how: Toast 8 crumpets until golden and spread with butter. Mix 200g grated cheddar with a spoon of English mustard and pile onto each crumpet. Grill until bubbling and golden. Serve hot on a plate for a hungry detective.

s.note: Soft boiled eggs wrapped in pork sausage, crumbed and fried
s.how: Boil 4 eggs for 6 minutes, cool and peel. Wrap each in 100g pork sausage mince. Roll in flour, beaten egg and panko, then fry at 170C for 6 minutes until golden. Halve and serve with English mustard, like a bar snack in a dodgy pub.

m.note: Lamb mince with carrots and peas under mash
m.how: Brown 800g lamb mince with a diced onion and 2 grated carrots. Add a cup of peas and a little water and simmer for 30 minutes until thick. Spread in a dish, top with mash from 1kg potatoes and plenty of butter and bake at 200C until golden.

w.note: Butter sponge layers with strawberry jam and whipped cream
w.how: Beat 200g butter with 200g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 200g self-raising flour. Bake in 2 tins at 180C for 25 minutes. Cool, then sandwich with strawberry jam and whipped cream. Dust the top with icing sugar and serve at half past four.

d.note: Earl Grey tea with honey and lemon juice, over ice
d.how: Steep 4 Earl Grey tea bags in 600ml boiling water for 5 minutes, remove and stir in 3 tbsp honey. Chill for 2 hours. Add the juice of 3 lemons. Fill 4 glasses with ice and lemon slices, pour in the tea to two thirds full and top with 300ml sparkling water. Serve with shortbread fingers.
